metadata.note: United Traction Company (Albany city streetcar lines). GEOMETRY CORRECTED 2026-08-24: the alignments were previously 4-6 point hand-placed sketches following roughly the right corridors but not the right streets -- the State Street line ran 200-500 m south of State Street along its whole length. All five are now routed along present-day street centrelines from OpenStreetMap, 96-100% of each within 25 m of a way carrying that street's name. Street centrelines are the right approximation for a street railway, but the routes have still NOT been verified against Sanborn fire insurance maps or period track maps, and the terminal points at each end are chosen from the street network rather than from a source. Headways remain illustrative placeholders based on typical urban streetcar service of the era, pending real timetable research (Official Guide of the Railways, UTC schedules). See albany_troy_trolley.geojson for the UTC's Albany-Troy interurban route.
sources_to_check: Fred Abele streetcar collection, New York State Library
Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps, Albany NY, 1890s-1930s
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Route extents and terminals are inferred from the street network, not from a source: where each car line actually began and ended, and how the State Street line continued west of Washington Park (which interrupts the street), are all unknown. Every headway is a placeholder and every speed is an estimate. No period track map has been consulted.
metadata.horsecar_audit: 2026-08-24: removed as part of a repo-wide horsecar audit. Removed here: segment 1890-1894 from utc-state-st (the segment labelled "horsecar era, pre-electrification"; the State Street line now begins in 1894). REPO RULE 5: this map shows MECHANICALLY powered rail -- horsecars and mule cars are out of scope, and a line's drawn years must start when it stopped using animals. Notes may still mention the animal era as context. See CLAUDE.md.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.speed_source: estimated: urban electric streetcar with frequent stops; unsourced
properties.geometry_source: Routed along present-day street centrelines from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass, by shortest path weighted to prefer ways carrying the street's own name. REPLACES the 4-6 point hand-placed sketch this feature previously carried, which was measurably off: the old State Street line ran 200-500 m south of the real State Street for its whole length. Drawn extent: Broadway at the river west up State Street to the east edge of Washington Park. 51 points, 1.31 mi.
properties.geometry_quality: STREET-CENTRELINE ROUTING, not a traced track alignment -- appropriate for a street railway, whose cars ran in the roadway, but which side of the street, the terminal loops and any short deviations are not verified against Sanborn or period track maps. No leg is a straight-line placeholder. State Street is interrupted by Washington Park in the street network, and no source has been found for how the car line continued west of the park, so the drawn line stops at the park's east edge. 100% of the drawn length lies within 25 m of a way named State Street. Traced 1.31 mi; no documented route mileage has been found for this car line to check it against. Previous sketch was 6 points, 1.22 mi.
